reason: The passage does not depict conflict between Hebrew and Egyptian peoples. Instead, it focuses on establishing a religious covenant between God and Israel at Mount Sinai (Exodus 19), followed by an internal religious crisis—the golden calf incident (Exodus 32)—which represents conflict between the Israelites and God/the divine law. While Egypt is referenced as the place of past deliverance ('מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם' - 'from the land of Egypt'), no actual conflict or confrontation between Hebrew and Egyptian nations is depicted or even described in this text. The conflict portrayed is religious and intra-communal, not national or external.
